sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the Danish-locale page (English text summarized) on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: 'Identify the main blocking session (head blocker)'; scenario 2, a sleeping SPID with open_transaction_count greater than zero, which a timeout or cancel does not end ('doesn't automatically roll back or commit the transaction'), resolved by the application (IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK, SET XACT_ABORT ON) and listed as 'No, but SPID can be killed'; a killed session is marked KILLED/ROLLBACK until the rollback ends; blocked_process_report in Extended Events with the threshold set by sp_configure ('By default, no blocked process reports are produced'). KILL WITH STATUSONLY is not on that page; to verify against the KILL reference.

brief.situation: You are the database administrator for Brookline Supply, a fictional wholesaler running SQL Server 2022 on an Azure virtual machine (sql-prod01). At 09:00 the service desk reports that order entry hangs: every save spins until it times out. Month-end invoicing starts at 09:30 and writes to the same Orders table.
handover: Nothing was deployed overnight. Two DBAs were doing archive tests on Sales this morning.
The blocked process threshold is 0 (off), so no blocked process reports exist yet.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the sessions on Sales and who waits on whom.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Invoicing starts at 09:30, 30 minutes after the report.

chain.label: sqlcmd: SELECT session_id, blocking_session_id, wait_type, wait_time FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0
chain.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.output:
dba@ops-jump:~$ sqlcmd -S sql-prod01 -d Sales -Q "SELECT session_id, blocking_session_id, wait_type, wait_time/1000 AS s FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0"
{unblocked ? "(0 rows affected)" : "session_id blocking_session_id wait_type  s
112        87                  LCK_M_IX   212
115        87                  LCK_M_IX   188
118        112                 LCK_M_IX   95
(3 rows affected)"}

effects.finding: Every chain ends at session 87, which is not in sys.dm_exec_requests itself: it is not running anything. It is the head blocker.

buffer.label: sqlcmd: sys.dm_exec_sessions and sys.dm_exec_input_buffer(87, NULL) for the head blocker
buffer.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.finding: Session 87 is sleeping with one open transaction: an archive test that began a transaction at 08:41 and never committed or rolled back. Its locks stay until it ends.

contact.label: Message J. Lee: is session 87's archive UPDATE meant to be kept?

effects.log: J. Lee: 'That was a test against the wrong window. Roll it back; nothing in it should stay.'

kill.label: KILL 87;  then KILL 87 WITH STATUSONLY
kill.available: not busy and (not killing and not restarted)

effects.output:
dba@ops-jump:~$ sqlcmd -S sql-prod01 -d Sales -Q "KILL 87"
dba@ops-jump:~$ sqlcmd -S sql-prod01 -d Sales -Q "KILL 87 WITH STATUSONLY"
SPID 87: transaction rollback in progress. Estimated rollback completion: 61%. Estimated time remaining: 40 seconds.

effects.log: Session 87 is marked KILLED/ROLLBACK; its UPDATE rolls back and its locks are released when the rollback ends.

killVictims.label: KILL 112; KILL 115; KILL 118  (the sessions that hang)
killVictims.available: not busy and (not victimsKilled and not unblocked)

effects.output:
dba@ops-jump:~$ sqlcmd -S sql-prod01 -d Sales -Q "KILL 112; KILL 115; KILL 118"
Commands completed successfully.

effects.log: Three users lose the order they were saving. Their retries queue behind session 87 again.

nolock.label: Ask the app team to add WITH (NOLOCK) to the order entry queries

effects.log: Reads stop waiting, but they now read uncommitted rows, including session 87's archived statuses. Writes still wait.

restart.label: Restart the SQL Server service on sql-prod01

effects.output:
dba@ops-jump:~$ ssh sql-prod01 'Restart-Service MSSQLSERVER -Force'
WARNING: Waiting for service 'SQL Server (MSSQLSERVER)' to stop...
Sales: recovery 41% complete (phase 2 of 3)...

effects.log: Every connection on the server drops, other databases included; Sales is in recovery for 35 minutes.

xe.label: Set blocked process threshold to 20 s and start an Extended Events session on blocked_process_report

effects.output:
dba@ops-jump:~$ sqlcmd -S sql-prod01 -d Sales -Q "EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'blocked process threshold (s)',20; RECONFIGURE; CREATE EVENT SESSION blocking ON SERVER ADD EVENT sqlserver.blocked_process_report ADD TARGET package0.event_file(SET filename='blocking'); ALTER EVENT SESSION blocking ON SERVER STATE=START"
Configuration option 'blocked process threshold (s)' changed from 0 to 20.

effects.log: The next blocking chain longer than 20 seconds leaves a report naming the head blocker.

options.label: A sleeping SSMS session (87) with an uncommitted archive UPDATE held locks on Orders; killed and rolled back with the owner's agreement

writeup.question: For the record: who was blocking, how you ended it, and how you will see it sooner next time.

parts.label: Head blocker
parts.criteria: Follows blocking_session_id to the head and reads its state and input buffer.
parts.modelAnswer: sys.dm_exec_requests showed every chain ending at 87; sys.dm_exec_sessions showed it sleeping with open_transaction_count 1 and the input buffer showed an uncommitted archive UPDATE from 08:41.

parts.label: Ended
parts.criteria: Kills the head blocker, not its victims, after checking with its owner, and knows the KILL rolls back.
parts.modelAnswer: J. Lee confirmed it was a test, so KILL 87 rolled the UPDATE back; WITH STATUSONLY showed the rollback progress. Killing 112-118 or restarting the service would have hurt users and not ended the cause.

parts.label: Next time
parts.criteria: Turns on the blocked process report and checks.
parts.modelAnswer: Blocked process threshold 20 s and an Extended Events session on blocked_process_report; the re-run showed no blocked requests before 09:30.

expertPath.text: sys.dm_exec_requests: every chain ends at 87; sys.dm_exec_sessions and the input buffer: sleeping, one open transaction, an archive UPDATE since 08:41.
J. Lee confirms it was a test; KILL 87 and WITH STATUSONLY until the rollback ends; re-run the blocking query.
Blocked process threshold 20 s and an Extended Events session on blocked_process_report.

restarted.headline: A restart ended everything, not just the blocker
restarted.body: One sleeping session held the locks. Restarting the service rolls it back the slow way, through crash recovery, and drops every other user and database with it.

invoiceMissed.headline: Invoicing could not start
invoiceMissed.body: The waiting sessions are victims. Follow blocking_session_id to the session that is not waiting on anyone, read what it holds, and end that one.

fixed.headline: Good: the head blocker, ended safely
fixed.body: You followed the chain to a sleeping session with an open transaction, checked what it held and whose it was, killed only it, and left a blocked process report so the next one names itself.

gaps.headline: Unblocked, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the input buffer, the owner's agreement, killed victims, a NOLOCK request, the check, or the blocked process report.

time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The waiting sessions all point, directly or through each other, to session 87, which is not running anything: the head blocker. sys.dm_exec_sessions shows it sleeping with open_transaction_count 1, and its input buffer shows an archive UPDATE begun at 08:41 and never committed, so its exclusive locks on Orders stay until the transaction ends. Its owner confirms it was a test, so KILL 87 rolls it back (WITH STATUSONLY shows the progress) and the locks go. Killing the waiting sessions loses users' orders and changes nothing; NOLOCK reads uncommitted data and does not help writes; restarting the service ends the blocker through crash recovery and drops everyone. Re-run the check, then set the blocked process threshold and capture blocked_process_report with Extended Events.
